reviews.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended The CSV failure behavior lacks the required mocked Robot regression verifying that earlier rows remain on stdout while the CLI still reports the decoding error.
1 open issue - [Add Robot regression for partial CSV output after decoding failure](https://github.com/stackql/stackql/pull/939#discussion_r4632186818) · New
What changed in this PR Extends #905’s partial-output handling so StackQL preserves buffered CSV rows when a later chunk fails to decode, while still returning the error. **Changes:** - Flushes buffered CSV output on decoding errors in both the mid-stream and EOF branches. - Adds a unit regression using a valid chunk followed by a malformed chunk. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `internal/​stackql/​output/​partial_table_test.go` | Adds a batched-stream helper and regression for retaining earlier CSV rows. | | `internal/​stackql/​output/​output.go` | Flushes CSV output before returning chunk-decoding errors. |
Review effort: Balanced
@pcbeingused333 I like this.  Please add a robot test.  Thank you kindly

review_comments.body: This changes user-visible CSV output on failure, but the only regression test invokes the writer directly with a synthetic stream. The repository requires a Robot regression for user-visible query behavior changes; unit tests alone do not cover the CLI's handling of partial stdout and the returned error. Add a mocked Robot scenario that produces a valid chunk followed by a decoding failure and asserts that earlier CSV rows remain on stdout while the failure is still reported.

@pcbeingused333 this is a valid idea from copilot.  Please do add one black box mocked `robot` framework test verifying this scenario, including that some standard python (just because we are in the robot stack) csv reader on error-aborted result set "just works" and can project eomething useful.

comments.body:
Thanks for the review. I tried to add a Robot regression for this path, but the decoding failure that #939 handles (an error from `tabulateResults`/`decodeRow` on a later chunk) is not reachable through the mocked HTTP provider: with the cursor mock serving a non-numeric value for an `integer` or `boolean` column on page 2, stackql passes the value through as text, so nothing fails and the row is printed. The stream-read failure case is already covered by the Robot test added in #905, and the new decode-failure branch is covered by the unit test `partial_table_test.go` (valid chunk followed by a malformed one). Is the unit test enough for this branch, or is there a mock/column type you would use to force a decode error end to end? I'm happy to add the Robot case if you point me to one.

This comment was prepared with the help of an AI coding assistant (Claude) and checked against a local build before posting.

@pcbeingused333  ahhhh this one is interesting indeed and I guess it must snowball.  I will merge this now and if you are keen then you can look at the follow up work in [issue 945](https://github.com/stackql/stackql/issues/945)
